improvements in diabetes, sleep apnea, hypertension, and 
CVD risk factors.14, 85, 88 For example, in a study of nearly 
8,000 patients who underwent RYGB surgery, there was a 40% 
reduction in mortality from such causes as coronary heart dis-
ease, diabetes, and cancer compared to the control group.94
Postoperative complications include pulmonary embolism, anas-
tomotic leaks, injury to the spleen, wound infection, 
and, rarely, death.9, 85, 95 However, a recent study of nearly 
5,000 patients who underwent bariatric surgery showed that
when performed by highly-skilled surgeons in high-volume 
centers, the risks of RYGB and the AGB were no greater than
gallbladder or hip-replacement surgery.88, 95 Among these patients, 
the overall risk of death was 0.3% and 4.3% experienced at least 
one major complication; however, these rates were greater in 
patients with very high BMI and who had a history of obesity-
related complications.95 Careful preoperative screening and educa-
tion will ensure that candidates for surgery meet the BMI require-
ments, are free of major psychopathology, have the physical and 
emotional stamina to tolerate the procedure, are willing to make
the necessary dietary and lifestyle changes, and are committed to 
long-term follow-up. Also important are long-term follow-up and
